turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good afternoon, Mr Krishnan. Please have a seat. What brings you in today?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Good afternoon, doctor. Actually speaking I have come only for a general check-up. My son Arjun is in Dubai and he keeps calling, Papa you are sixty-three now, kindly go and get yourself checked, so I came. Nothing major as such.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): A routine check-up, I follow. Have you noticed any trouble yourself, or is it only because your son asked?

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Purely that only, doctor. I am keeping well, I do my walking in the colony in the morning, I take my BP tablet, I am managing. The lift in our building has been out since last month, that is a separate headache, but health-wise I am alright.

[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, if I may. I stay with him, I am Geeta, the carer. He is not saying the full thing. Since some weeks he is very slow on the stairs, and one day he held the railing and just stood.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Geeta, that is not fair. I was only catching my breath, the stairs are steep and I was carrying the milk packet. I am not having chest pain. I told you also, no pain.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright, so you are saying there is no chest pain. When you are climbing, is there any tight feeling or pressure, or only breathlessness?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no chest pain, doctor. Breathlessness also, only a little, like any person of my age. I stop and I am fine.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): And if you walk fast, on the flat road, same thing or no?

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Walking fast... well, actually, if I walk fast to catch the bus there is a kind of tightness. Not pain. Like someone is holding the chest from inside. I should have said that earlier, it is tightness only.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tightness, not a sharp pain. Where exactly does it sit, and does it go to the arm or the jaw?

[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Centre of the chest, doctor, behind the breastbone you can say, and it does not go to the arm or the jaw. I kept checking myself, no sweating, no vomiting sensation. It comes, I stand for one or two minutes, and it goes. Same thing when I climb to the second floor.
[SEG0013] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It has been there for about three weeks, doctor. He will say less.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Not three weeks, Geeta. Um, I noticed it properly only from last week, after the lift broke. Before that I was not climbing so much. Maybe ten days, I cannot be exact.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): So the timing is a bit unclear, somewhere between ten days and three weeks, and we will not pin it down. Any palpitations, a thumping in the chest?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No palpitations, doctor. Nothing like that.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any blackout, any giddiness, any swelling of the feet?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Giddiness no. Feet are not swollen. I look every night because my brother had that, but mine are normal.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): You mentioned your brother. Any heart problem in the family?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): My elder brother had a bypass at fifty-eight, doctor. Father had BP, he passed at seventy-two, not a heart attack as such. Mother was sugar.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thank you. Now the tablets. Which BP tablet, and what strength?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine, doctor. I take it every morning after breakfast, since four years, for the BP. The strip says 5 mg, I am very particular, I don't change the dose myself.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): In the previous note here it is written amlodipine 5 mg once daily. Geeta, is that what you give him?
[SEG0024] person_3 (CAREGIVER): No, doctor, that note is old. The strip in the cupboard is 10 mg. I give him one 10 mg tablet every morning, and I have been doing that for months.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Geeta, you are mixing it up with the spare strip. My regular one is 5 mg. The 10 mg was bought by mistake by my son last year and it is just sitting there. I take 5.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): So the two of you are not agreeing on 5 or 10, and I will not write a dose until we see the strip. Please bring the actual packet next time. What about aspirin?

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Aspirin 75, the small one. The doctor had said daily, but honestly I take it on and off. If I feel fine I skip two three days, and last week I took maybe three tablets only. The stomach becomes a little heavy if I take it daily, so I avoid.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): So it was advised every day, but you are missing doses, and we cannot be sure how many you actually take. Any other tablet, cholesterol or anything, that you stopped?

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Atorvastatin, doctor, 10 mg at night. I stopped it in March, the calves were cramping at night, so I left it. After stopping, the cramps went away in a week or so, and I did not restart.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stopped in March, and not taking it now. Was a beta blocker, metoprolol, ever started?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): They wrote metoprolol once in the old clinic, but I never took even one tablet. I was worried it would make me slow. So that one I never started, you can ignore it.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will not put that down as a medicine you take. Any allergy to a medicine or a food?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No allergy, doctor. Penicillin also I have taken in the past for a tooth, no problem. Food also nothing.

[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. Let me check you now. Blood pressure today is 148 over 92, pulse 76, regular. Oxygen is 98 percent. Chest is clear with no added sounds, heart sounds are normal with no murmur, and there is no swelling at the ankles.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): 148 is a bit high, no, doctor? At home last Sunday I measured 136 over 84, and I wrote it in my diary, even the time, 7.30 in the morning, before tea.

[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Home and clinic can differ, and I am recording today's reading. Let me say back what I have heard, and you correct me if I slip. You came for a check-up, and there is a tight feeling in the centre of the chest when you climb stairs or walk fast, which settles if you rest for a minute or two. You are not describing pain in the arm, sweating, vomiting, palpitations, giddiness or swollen feet, you take a blood pressure tablet every morning but we are not sure if it is 5 or 10 mg of amlodipine, aspirin 75 only on some days, you stopped atorvastatin 10 mg in March, and your brother had a bypass, is that fair?

[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor, that is correct. Only one small thing, the tightness is more on the stairs than on the flat road, though walking fast also brings it. And I am a retired school clerk, I sit a lot, that also maybe.
[SEG0038] person_3 (CAREGIVER): And he still climbs, doctor. I tell him to use the neighbour's lift and he will not listen.

[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): I understand. My working impression is that this exertional tightness may be angina, but that is not confirmed. I want an ECG today, and blood tests, haemoglobin, kidney function, fasting sugar, and a cholesterol profile.

[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): ECG I can do now itself? I have not eaten since morning, only one banana at 6, so the fasting sugar should be alright, no? I was thinking I will have lunch after this, there is a small place near the bus stop and they make very good idli.

[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): One banana means it is not a true fast, so we will still send the sugar, but I will note that you had a banana. Please have the ECG and the bloods today before you go for idli. I am also asking you to rest when the tightness comes, and not to hurry on the stairs till we know more. If it comes at rest, or with sweating, or does not settle in a few minutes, go straight to emergency, do not wait for me.

[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Understood, doctor. I will bring the amlodipine strip also next time so you can see whether it is 5 or 10. And I will try not to skip the aspirin, though my stomach does not like it.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): We will look at the stomach separately if it keeps troubling you. Come back in one week for the results, whether you feel well or not. Reception will book it.

spec.situation: Man or woman 50-70 who comes 'for a check-up' and only slowly admits a tight feeling in the chest when climbing stairs or walking fast; first denies chest pain, later describes the tightness. Takes a BP tablet and aspirin on and off. Doctor orders ECG and bloods.
features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

bad.reason: Aspirin 75 is current, but frequency once daily is not actual; he takes it on and off.
bad.text: aspirin (dose=75 mg, frequency=once daily, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: Dose, night, discontinued, patient-supported; indication cholesterol not stated.
bad.text: atorvastatin (dose=10 mg, frequency=at night, indication=cholesterol, status=discontinued, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Current aspirin use is recorded wrongly as once daily; the patient said aspirin 75 mg was advised daily but he actually takes it only on and off, skipping two to three days at a time and taking only about three tablets in the last week.
Metoprolol was prescribed in the past but the patient never started it and never took even one tablet.
No chest pain was specifically asked and denied; the symptom was described as tightness rather than pain.
Breathlessness on exertion was further characterised as occurring only a little with climbing stairs and improving when he stops.
The chest tightness is more prominent on stairs than on flat ground, although fast walking can also bring it on.
The patient denied blackout/syncope when asked.
Allergy history included specific tolerance of penicillin in the past and no food allergies.
The patient reported a home blood pressure reading of 136/84 taken last Sunday at 7:30 in the morning before tea.
For the planned blood tests, the doctor noted that the patient had eaten a banana at 6 am, so the fasting sugar would not be a true fasting sample.
The doctor said to come back in one week for the results whether he feels well or not.

omissions.text: Amlodipine dose is recorded incompletely: the patient specifically said his strip says 5 mg and the caregiver specifically said she gives 10 mg every morning; the doctor said he would not record a dose until the actual strip is seen.
Aspirin 75 mg was advised as a daily medicine, but the patient reported nonadherence with only about three tablets taken in the last week because daily use causes stomach heaviness.
Atorvastatin 10 mg was stopped in March because of nocturnal calf cramps, and the patient did not restart it after the cramps resolved within about a week.
Metoprolol had been prescribed previously but the patient never started it and never took even one tablet.
The chest tightness is described as retrosternal/behind the breastbone and specifically as a holding sensation rather than sharp pain.
The patient said the exertional tightness is more prominent on stairs than on flat walking.
There was no blackout/syncope.
The patient denied medication and food allergy, and specifically reported prior penicillin exposure without any problem.
Family history detail: father died at age 72 and this was not thought to be a heart attack.
Home blood pressure was measured at 136/84 at 7:30 am before tea last Sunday, not just an undated home BP value.
The doctor advised that if aspirin-related stomach symptoms continue, they will assess the stomach separately.
Follow-up instruction was to return in one week for the results whether he feels well or not.
